mainEntity.name: Who runs EVE Women and Fertility Clinic?

acceptedAnswer.text: EVE was founded in December 2025 by Dr. Swati Shree, a reproductive medicine specialist with an MRCOG (UK), a DNB in obstetrics and gynaecology and a fellowship in reproductive medicine. She personally leads the clinic and sees every patient herself.

mainEntity.name: Where is EVE located?

acceptedAnswer.text: EVE is on the 1st floor of LG Complex Towers in Gunjur, Bangalore 560087, in East Bengaluru. It is close to Varthur, Balagere, Whitefield and Sarjapur Road. See Plan your visit for directions and parking.

mainEntity.name: Is EVE a hospital?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. EVE is an outpatient clinic. You do not stay overnight. Consultations, scans, tests and clinic procedures happen here. For procedures that need a hospital or a registered ART laboratory, Dr. Swati explains where it will be done before you decide.

mainEntity.name: Does EVE treat only fertility problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. EVE also looks after PCOS, endometriosis, menstrual problems, fibroids, thyroid issues linked to pregnancy, early pregnancy scans, cervical screening, contraception counselling and menopause care. You do not need to be trying to conceive to see Dr. Swati.

mainEntity.name: Do you accept patients from outside Bangalore?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many couples travel for the first evaluation. We try to complete tests in as few visits as possible and plan follow-up with you. See Coming from outside Bangalore for a visit plan.

mainEntity.name: How can I check that the clinic and doctor are registered?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dr. Swati's registration is with the Karnataka Medical Council, number DLH20090000353KTK, and can be checked on the National Medical Commission's Indian Medical Register. The clinic's ART registration appears in the footer and on the Patient Rights page.

itemListElement.name: Adenomyosis and Fertility Symptoms and Treatment

@graph.name: Adenomyosis and Fertility Symptoms and Treatment
@graph.headline: Adenomyosis and Fertility Symptoms and Treatment

mainEntity.name: Can you get pregnant with adenomyosis?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many women with adenomyosis conceive, though the condition may reduce the chance of pregnancy or raise miscarriage risk in some. A fertility evaluation helps decide on treatment and timing.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between adenomyosis and endometriosis?

acceptedAnswer.text: In adenomyosis, endometrial-like tissue grows into the muscle wall of the uterus, while in endometriosis it grows outside the womb. They can occur together and cause overlapping symptoms.

mainEntity.name: How is adenomyosis diagnosed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Doctors use symptoms, pelvic examination and imaging such as transvaginal ultrasound or MRI. Imaging shows changes in the uterine wall that suggest adenomyosis.

mainEntity.name: Can adenomyosis be treated before IVF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some patients benefit from medical treatment or specific protocols before embryo transfer, and surgery may be considered selectively. Your specialist will individualise the plan.

mainEntity.name: Does adenomyosis go away after menopause?

acceptedAnswer.text: Symptoms usually improve after menopause because hormones that stimulate the tissue decline. Treatment for symptoms during the reproductive years depends on your goals.

@graph.name: AMH vs Egg Quality: What Is the Difference?
@graph.headline: AMH vs Egg Quality: What Is the Difference?

mainEntity.name: Does AMH measure egg quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AMH estimates how many eggs remain in the ovaries. It does not measure whether those eggs are healthy.

mainEntity.name: What determines egg quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Age is the main factor. As women age, more eggs carry chromosomal errors. Lifestyle and some medical conditions may also play a role.

mainEntity.name: Can you have low AMH and good egg quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Younger women with low AMH may have fewer eggs, but those eggs can still be of good quality.

mainEntity.name: Is there a test for egg quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no direct test. Egg quality is inferred from age and observed in IVF through fertilisation and embryo development. Genetic testing of embryos can provide additional information.

mainEntity.name: Can I improve my egg quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Age-related changes cannot be reversed, but not smoking, limiting alcohol, a healthy weight and managing health conditions support reproductive health.

itemListElement.name: Blastocyst Transfer and Embryo Grading Explained

@graph.name: Blastocyst Transfer and Embryo Grading Explained
@graph.headline: Blastocyst Transfer and Embryo Grading Explained

mainEntity.name: What is a blastocyst?

acceptedAnswer.text: A blastocyst is an embryo that has developed for about five to six days and formed a fluid-filled cavity with an inner cell mass and an outer layer. It is the stage at which embryos naturally implant in the womb.

mainEntity.name: What does embryo grade 4AA mean?

acceptedAnswer.text: The number describes how expanded the blastocyst is, and the letters rate the inner cell mass and trophectoderm, with A being the best. A 4AA blastocyst is a well-expanded, high-quality embryo, though grading does not guarantee success.

mainEntity.name: Can a low-grade embryo result in a healthy baby?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Lower-grade embryos can implant and lead to healthy pregnancies, although the average chance is lower than for higher grades. Grading is only one factor among many.

mainEntity.name: Is day 5 transfer better than day 3 transfer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Day 5 transfer can help select embryos with better developmental potential in some patients, but it is not better for everyone, especially when few embryos are available. Your specialist will recommend the best timing.

mainEntity.name: Why do some embryos stop growing before day 5?

acceptedAnswer.text: Embryos may stop developing because of chromosomal or other abnormalities that are common in human embryos. It is a natural selection process and does not usually reflect anything done by the patient.

itemListElement.name: Blocked Fallopian Tubes Symptoms, HSG and Treatment

@graph.name: Blocked Fallopian Tubes Symptoms, HSG and Treatment
@graph.headline: Blocked Fallopian Tubes Symptoms, HSG and Treatment

mainEntity.name: Can you get pregnant with one blocked fallopian tube?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, many women conceive with one open tube, though the chance may be reduced depending on other factors. Your doctor will assess the open tube and the rest of your fertility picture.

mainEntity.name: Is HSG painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many women feel cramping similar to period pain during the dye injection, and some feel little. Pain medicine taken beforehand and a gentle technique help. Discomfort usually settles soon after.

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to do an HSG?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is usually done after the period has stopped and before ovulation, in the first half of the cycle, to avoid disturbing a possible pregnancy. Your doctor will give exact timing.

mainEntity.name: Can blocked tubes open on their own?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some temporary blockage can clear, and flushing during HSG may open minor obstructions in some women, but established damage does not usually resolve on its own. Your doctor will advise next steps.

mainEntity.name: Is IVF the only option for blocked tubes?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Some tubal problems can be treated surgically, but when damage is severe or surgery is unlikely to help, IVF is usually advised because it bypasses the tubes. The best option depends on your situation.

@graph.name: Can Endometriosis Cause Infertility?
@graph.headline: Can Endometriosis Cause Infertility?

mainEntity.name: Can I get pregnant naturally with endometriosis?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many women do, especially when the disease is mild, the tubes are open and egg reserve is good. If pregnancy does not happen within the recommended time for your age, a fertility specialist can suggest next steps.

mainEntity.name: Does endometriosis affect egg quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: It may affect the pelvic environment and, in some women, ovarian reserve. The effect on egg quality is still being studied. Age remains the most important factor for egg quality in most women.

mainEntity.name: Does surgery for endometriosis improve fertility?

acceptedAnswer.text: In some women, removing endometriosis or scar tissue may help. Surgery on ovarian cysts must be planned carefully because it can reduce egg reserve. Your doctor will weigh the benefits and risks for your situation.

mainEntity.name: How is endometriosis diagnosed?

acceptedAnswer.text: Doctors use your symptoms, a pelvic examination and ultrasound. Endometriomas and deep disease can often be seen on scans. Laparoscopy can confirm the diagnosis in uncertain cases and treat it at the same time.

mainEntity.name: Is IVF needed for endometriosis?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. IVF may be considered when tubes are damaged, egg reserve is low, age is a concern or other treatments have not worked. Many women with mild disease conceive without IVF.

mainEntity.name: Should I see a specialist if I have painful periods and cannot conceive?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Painful periods, pain during sex or pelvic pain along with difficulty conceiving can point to endometriosis. A fertility specialist can evaluate both pain and fertility together and plan suitable care.

@graph.name: Can You Get Pregnant Naturally With Low AMH?
@graph.headline: Can You Get Pregnant Naturally With Low AMH?

mainEntity.name: Can I get pregnant with low AMH naturally?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many women with low AMH conceive naturally, especially if they are younger, ovulate regularly and have no other fertility issues. Seeking specialist advice helps plan timelines.

mainEntity.name: Does low AMH mean poor egg quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AMH reflects the number of eggs, not their quality. Egg quality is mainly related to age.

mainEntity.name: What is considered a low AMH level?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ranges vary by laboratory and age. Your fertility specialist will interpret your AMH in the context of your age, antral follicle count and other findings.

mainEntity.name: Can supplements increase AMH?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no strong evidence that supplements significantly raise AMH or egg numbers. Discuss any supplements with your doctor before taking them.

mainEntity.name: Should I freeze my eggs if my AMH is low?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you are not planning pregnancy soon, egg freezing may be worth discussing. Low AMH may mean fewer eggs retrieved, so earlier consideration is often advised.

@graph.name: Early Pregnancy After IVF: When to Call Your Doctor
@graph.headline: Early Pregnancy After IVF: When to Call Your Doctor

mainEntity.name: Is bleeding in early IVF pregnancy always a miscarriage?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Light spotting is fairly common and many pregnancies continue normally. Heavy bleeding, clots or bleeding with pain need prompt assessment. Always inform your clinic about any bleeding.

mainEntity.name: Can ectopic pregnancy happen after IVF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, although the embryo is placed in the uterus, it can sometimes implant elsewhere, most often in a tube. This is why early ultrasound is done. Severe or one-sided pain needs urgent checking.

mainEntity.name: What is OHSS in early pregnancy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome is a reaction to fertility medicines that causes swollen ovaries and fluid buildup. Pregnancy hormones can worsen it. Watch for rapid swelling, breathlessness and reduced urine.

mainEntity.name: Are cramps normal after a positive IVF test?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mild cramps similar to period pain are common as the uterus grows. Severe, sharp or one-sided pain, or cramps with heavy bleeding, should be checked quickly by your doctor.

mainEntity.name: Should I go to the emergency room or call my clinic?

acceptedAnswer.text: For severe pain, fainting, heavy bleeding or breathlessness, go to emergency care immediately. For milder symptoms, call your clinic for advice. Keep your clinic's emergency number handy.

mainEntity.name: Can I travel during early IVF pregnancy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Short, comfortable travel is often fine once the pregnancy is confirmed in the uterus. Check with your doctor first, especially if you have bleeding, OHSS or a multiple pregnancy.

@graph.name: Egg Freezing: Who Should Consider It?
@graph.headline: Egg Freezing: Who Should Consider It?

mainEntity.name: What is the best age to freeze eggs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Freezing at a younger age, often in the late twenties or early thirties, generally gives better outcomes because egg quality is higher. Women in their mid to late thirties can still benefit, but may need more eggs.

mainEntity.name: How many eggs should I freeze?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your age and goals. Younger women usually need fewer eggs for a similar chance of pregnancy. Your specialist will suggest a target based on your age and test results.

mainEntity.name: Is egg freezing painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: The injections can cause mild discomfort and bloating. Egg collection is done under sedation, so you should not feel pain during the procedure. Mild cramps may occur for a day or two afterward.

mainEntity.name: How long can eggs stay frozen?

acceptedAnswer.text: With vitrification, eggs can remain frozen for many years without losing quality. Storage limits may be governed by local regulations and clinic policies, so ask your clinic.

mainEntity.name: Does egg freezing affect my future fertility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Egg freezing does not use up your remaining eggs faster or cause early menopause. The medicines help eggs that would have been lost that month to mature.

mainEntity.name: Can I freeze embryos instead of eggs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, if you have a partner or use donor sperm. Embryo freezing is an established option. Egg freezing offers more flexibility if you do not yet have a partner. Your specialist can explain both options.

@graph.name: Egg Quality After 35: What You Can and Cannot Change
@graph.headline: Egg Quality After 35: What You Can and Cannot Change

mainEntity.name: Can I improve my egg quality after 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: You cannot reverse age-related decline, but you can support overall egg health by quitting smoking, limiting alcohol, keeping a healthy weight and managing health conditions. These steps help fertility in general.

mainEntity.name: Is there a test for egg quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no direct test before eggs are collected. AMH and antral follicle count measure egg numbers. During IVF, embryo development and genetic testing give more information about egg quality.

mainEntity.name: Do supplements like CoQ10 improve egg quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some studies suggest a possible benefit, but evidence is limited. CoQ10 is not a proven cure. Speak with your doctor before taking any supplement, especially during fertility treatment.

mainEntity.name: Does good AMH mean good egg quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AMH shows egg quantity, not quality. A woman can have a normal AMH and still have age-related changes in egg quality. Age is the strongest predictor of egg quality.

mainEntity.name: Can diet improve egg quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: A balanced diet supports overall health and fertility, but no single food has been proven to improve egg quality. Focus on whole foods, vegetables, protein and healthy fats rather than special fertility diets.

mainEntity.name: Should I freeze my eggs to protect egg quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Egg freezing preserves eggs at their current quality, which may help if you plan to delay pregnancy. It works best at younger ages. A specialist can discuss whether it suits your plans.

@graph.name: Embryo Implantation After IVF: Timeline and Signs
@graph.headline: Embryo Implantation After IVF: Timeline and Signs

mainEntity.name: How soon does implantation happen after embryo transfer?

acceptedAnswer.text: After a day 5 blastocyst transfer, implantation usually begins within about 1 to 3 days. After a day 3 transfer, it may take a few extra days. hCG then starts rising in the blood.

mainEntity.name: Is implantation bleeding common after IVF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some women notice light spotting, but many do not. Spotting can also come from progesterone or the transfer itself. It does not confirm pregnancy. Inform your clinic about any bleeding.

mainEntity.name: Can I feel the embryo implanting?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most women do not feel anything during implantation. Mild cramps may occur but are usually due to medicines or the uterus settling. Feeling nothing is completely normal.

mainEntity.name: When should I take a pregnancy test after embryo transfer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most clinics recommend a blood hCG test about 9 to 12 days after transfer. Testing earlier can give false positive or false negative results. Follow your clinic's advice.

mainEntity.name: Does bed rest help implantation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Research does not show that strict bed rest improves implantation. Light, normal activity is usually fine. Avoid heavy lifting and intense workouts if your doctor advises it.

mainEntity.name: Can stress stop implantation?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no strong evidence that everyday stress prevents implantation. The wait is stressful for most couples. Gentle activities, rest and emotional support can help you feel better during this time.

@graph.name: Endometriosis and IVF: When Is IVF Considered?
@graph.headline: Endometriosis and IVF: When Is IVF Considered?

mainEntity.name: Is IVF successful with endometriosis?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many women with endometriosis conceive with IVF. Outcomes depend mostly on age, egg reserve and embryo quality. Your specialist can explain what to expect based on your own test results rather than general figures.

mainEntity.name: Should I remove endometriosis cysts before IVF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Surgery can reduce egg reserve. Small or medium cysts are often left alone. Surgery may be considered if cysts are very large, painful, block egg collection or look unusual on a scan.

mainEntity.name: Does endometriosis affect embryo quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: Research is ongoing. Some studies suggest a small effect, while others show similar embryo quality. Age remains the most important factor. Your embryologist will assess embryo development in your cycle.

mainEntity.name: Can endometriosis get worse during IVF?

acceptedAnswer.text: IVF medicines raise hormone levels for a short time, but this rarely causes lasting worsening. Some women notice temporary pain. Your doctor will monitor you and manage any symptoms.

mainEntity.name: Is frozen embryo transfer better for endometriosis?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some specialists prefer frozen transfer in selected cases, after preparing the uterus with medicines. Evidence is still evolving. The choice depends on your response to stimulation and your doctor's assessment.

mainEntity.name: How soon should I move to IVF with endometriosis?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on age, egg reserve, tubal status and previous treatments. Women over 35 or with low reserve may be advised to consider IVF sooner. A fertility specialist can set the right timeline.

mainEntity.name: Can I get pregnant if I have endometriosis?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many women with endometriosis get pregnant, some naturally and some with treatment. How likely it is for you depends on your age, how advanced the disease is, whether your tubes are open, your egg reserve and your partner's sperm. A fertility specialist looks at all of these together before suggesting whether to keep trying, try IUI or go straight to IVF.

mainEntity.name: Does endometriosis reduce AMH levels?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can, mainly when there are chocolate cysts (endometriomas) on the ovaries. Removing those cysts surgically may lower AMH further, since some healthy ovarian tissue often comes out with them. AMH reflects how many eggs you have, not how healthy they are. A low result doesn't mean pregnancy is impossible, though it may push your doctor to start treatment sooner.

mainEntity.name: Is surgery necessary before IVF if I have endometriosis?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually not. Guidelines don't routinely recommend removing a chocolate cyst just to improve IVF results, because the operation can reduce egg reserve. Surgery may still make sense if pain is severe, the cyst is large or looks unusual on scans, or it sits in the way of egg collection. Your fertility doctor will help you weigh this.

mainEntity.name: Is IUI or IVF better for endometriosis?

acceptedAnswer.text: That depends on your situation. IUI with ovulation induction may be tried for minimal or mild endometriosis, provided at least one tube is open and the semen analysis is normal. IVF is more often advised for moderate to severe disease, blocked tubes, low egg reserve, age over 35, sperm problems, or when earlier treatment hasn't resulted in pregnancy.

mainEntity.name: Can endometriosis be seen on an ultrasound?

acceptedAnswer.text: Partly. A transvaginal ultrasound picks up chocolate cysts and adenomyosis quite well, and an experienced sonologist can spot some deep endometriosis. The small patches scattered on the pelvic lining usually don't show up. So a normal scan doesn't fully rule it out. If symptoms carry on, an MRI or a diagnostic laparoscopy may be suggested.

mainEntity.name: Will taking hormonal pills for endometriosis help me conceive later?

acceptedAnswer.text: They won't improve your fertility. Hormonal pills and similar medicines ease pain and may slow the disease, but they stop ovulation while you're taking them, and they don't raise your chances once you stop. They're useful for keeping symptoms under control until you're ready to try. Check with your doctor before starting or stopping any of them.

mainEntity.name: Is severe period pain always endometriosis?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Severe period pain can have other causes, such as adenomyosis, fibroids or pelvic infection. However, pain that disrupts daily life should be checked. A doctor can find the cause and suggest the right treatment.

mainEntity.name: Can endometriosis be seen on ultrasound?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ovarian cysts called endometriomas and some deep endometriosis can be seen on a good-quality ultrasound. Small surface patches may not be visible. Laparoscopy may be used if the diagnosis is unclear.

mainEntity.name: At what age does endometriosis start?

acceptedAnswer.text: Symptoms often begin in the teens or twenties, sometimes with the first periods. Many women are diagnosed later because symptoms were dismissed. Teenagers with severe period pain also deserve evaluation.

mainEntity.name: Can endometriosis cause pain outside periods?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Many women have pelvic or lower back pain at other times in the cycle, pain during sex or pain while passing stools. Pain patterns vary from person to person.

mainEntity.name: Does endometriosis run in families?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can. Women whose mother or sister has endometriosis have a higher chance of developing it. If you have a family history and painful periods, mention it to your doctor.

mainEntity.name: Can endometriosis go away after pregnancy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Symptoms may improve during pregnancy and breastfeeding because of hormonal changes, but endometriosis often returns afterward. Pregnancy is not a treatment. Long-term management depends on your symptoms and plans.

mainEntity.name: What is the most common cause of female infertility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Problems with ovulation are among the most frequent causes, and PCOS is a leading reason ovulation becomes irregular. Blocked fallopian tubes, endometriosis, fibroids or polyps in the uterus, and the drop in egg reserve that comes with age are also common. Many couples have more than one factor, and sperm problems often play a part too, so both partners should be tested.

mainEntity.name: Can a woman with regular periods still be infertile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Regular periods usually mean you're ovulating, which is a good sign, but they don't rule everything out. Blocked tubes, endometriosis, polyps, low ovarian reserve or a sperm problem in your partner can all exist alongside a perfectly regular cycle. If pregnancy hasn't happened in the expected time, testing is still worth doing.

mainEntity.name: Which tests are used to check female fertility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most evaluations include blood tests for FSH, LH, estradiol, thyroid and prolactin, plus an AMH test to estimate egg reserve. A transvaginal ultrasound looks at the uterus and ovaries, and an HSG or HyCoSy checks whether the tubes are open. A follicular study or progesterone test confirms ovulation. The male partner should have a semen analysis alongside these.

mainEntity.name: Can female infertility be treated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes. Thyroid and prolactin problems usually respond to medicine, ovulation can be helped with tablets or injections, and some uterine problems can be corrected with a short procedure. IUI and IVF are options when simpler steps aren't enough. Treatment improves the chance of pregnancy, though results depend on age, diagnosis and other personal factors.

mainEntity.name: How long should we try before seeing a fertility doctor?

acceptedAnswer.text: The general advice is 12 months of regular unprotected sex if you're under 35, and six months if you're between 35 and 40. Over 40, it's sensible to see a doctor straight away. Go sooner if your periods are irregular, you have PCOS or endometriosis, you've had a pelvic infection, or you've had repeated miscarriages.

mainEntity.name: Does low AMH mean I can't get pregnant?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Low AMH means your ovaries hold fewer eggs than average for your age. It doesn't measure egg quality and doesn't rule out pregnancy, and many women with low AMH conceive either naturally or with treatment. Doctors mainly use AMH to judge how your ovaries may respond to fertility medicines and how soon to start treatment.

mainEntity.name: Where can I get a fertility consultation in East Bangalore?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you live in Gunjur, Varthur, Whitefield, Sarjapur Road or nearby, you can see Dr. Swati Shree at EVE Women and Fertility Clinic in Gunjur. The clinic provides fertility assessment, counselling, ovulation induction, follicle monitoring and IUI. When IVF is needed, Dr. Swati Shree guides treatment through her partner fertility centres in Bangalore.

mainEntity.name: Can stress cause infertility in women?

acceptedAnswer.text: Stress by itself is rarely the main cause, and feeling anxious doesn't mean you caused the problem. Severe stress combined with very low food intake or intense exercise can sometimes disturb ovulation. More often it works the other way round, with infertility causing the stress. Counselling, rest and honest conversations with your partner can make treatment easier to get through.

mainEntity.name: What tests are done for female infertility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common tests include AMH, transvaginal ultrasound with antral follicle count, hormone tests such as FSH, LH, oestradiol, TSH and prolactin, progesterone to confirm ovulation and HSG to check the tubes.

mainEntity.name: What does a low AMH mean?

mainEntity.name: Is the HSG test painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many women feel cramping similar to period pain during HSG. Taking pain relief beforehand as advised can help. Discomfort usually settles quickly.

mainEntity.name: When should I get fertility tests?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually after 12 months of trying under 35, after 6 months at 35 or older, and earlier with irregular periods, endometriosis, previous pelvic surgery or age over 40.

mainEntity.name: Does my partner need testing too?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Male factors contribute to many cases of infertility. A semen analysis is usually done at the same time as female testing.

mainEntity.name: Is it harder to get pregnant after 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can take longer because both egg quantity and quality decline with age. Many women still conceive naturally. Seeking help after 6 months without pregnancy helps avoid unnecessary delay.

mainEntity.name: Why should I see a specialist after 6 months if I am over 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: Time matters more as fertility declines with age. Earlier evaluation can find treatable problems sooner and allows more treatment options while egg reserve is still adequate.

mainEntity.name: Does a normal AMH mean my fertility is fine after 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: A normal AMH suggests good egg quantity for your age, but it does not measure egg quality. Age remains the most important factor for egg quality. Your doctor will consider all results together.

mainEntity.name: Does miscarriage risk increase after 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The risk of miscarriage rises with age, mainly due to more chromosomal changes in eggs. Good antenatal care and early monitoring can help, and many pregnancies after 35 are healthy.

mainEntity.name: Should I consider IVF straight away after 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Many women conceive naturally or with simpler treatments. IVF may be recommended sooner if there are other factors like low egg reserve, blocked tubes or male factor problems.

mainEntity.name: Can lifestyle changes improve fertility after 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: Healthy habits support overall fertility and pregnancy health, but they cannot reverse age-related changes in eggs. Stopping smoking, keeping a healthy weight and managing health conditions are still worthwhile.

mainEntity.name: Is it hard to get pregnant after 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: It usually takes longer after 35, but plenty of women still conceive naturally. The main reason for the change is that fewer eggs remain and more of them carry chromosomal errors. If you're between 35 and 39 and haven't conceived after six months of trying, it's sensible to see a fertility specialist and get both partners tested.

mainEntity.name: What is a good AMH level at 35 or 40?

acceptedAnswer.text: AMH drops naturally with age, and labs use slightly different reference ranges, so a single number means little on its own. Your doctor will read it alongside your age, antral follicle count and other results. Low AMH suggests fewer eggs are left. It says nothing about egg quality and doesn't mean pregnancy is impossible.

mainEntity.name: Can I improve my egg quality after 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: Age-related changes in egg quality can't be reversed. What you can do is support your overall health by not smoking, cutting down on alcohol, eating regular balanced meals, staying active and keeping conditions like thyroid disease under control. Many supplements claim to help, but the evidence is thin, so check with your doctor first.

mainEntity.name: Should I try IUI or go straight to IVF after 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: That depends on your test results and how long you've been trying. A few IUI cycles can make sense if your tubes are open, your reserve is reasonable and sperm counts are adequate. After about 38 to 40, or if tubes are blocked, reserve is low or there's a significant sperm problem, IVF is usually discussed earlier.

mainEntity.name: Is egg freezing worth it at 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be, if you want to delay pregnancy. Eggs frozen at 35 generally give better chances later than eggs frozen in your 40s. Freezing doesn't guarantee a baby, and how many eggs you'd need varies from woman to woman. Ovarian reserve testing and a consultation will help you decide whether it's right for you.

mainEntity.name: Does my husband's age matter when trying to conceive?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, although usually less than a woman's age does. Older men can have lower semen quality and more sperm DNA damage. Male factors play a part in a large number of couples who struggle to conceive, at any age. A semen analysis is simple and painless and should be done early in the evaluation.

mainEntity.name: Which fertility test should I do first?

acceptedAnswer.text: Usually a pelvic ultrasound with an antral follicle count, an AMH blood test, thyroid and prolactin tests, and a semen analysis for the male partner. The tubal check follows at the right cycle day. Dr. Swati orders what fits your history, so you do only tests that help.

mainEntity.name: Can I do an AMH test on any day?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. AMH varies little through the cycle, so it can be tested on any day. Some other hormones, such as FSH and estradiol, are best on day 2 or 3. The scan for antral follicle count is also done early in the cycle.

mainEntity.name: Is a normal semen analysis enough to rule out male factor?

acceptedAnswer.text: A normal result is reassuring, but sperm counts vary. If your partner's result is borderline or if fertility is still a problem, a repeat test is sensible. The test does not show how well sperm function in fertilisation.

mainEntity.name: Does a low AMH mean I cannot get pregnant?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AMH shows how many eggs remain, not how good they are. Many women with low AMH conceive. It does mean that time may be shorter and that fewer eggs may be collected in IVF. Dr. Swati advises on timing.

mainEntity.name: Do I need all these tests?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. Dr. Swati chooses tests after hearing your history. Some couples need fewer, and some need more. If something is not helpful for you, she will tell you, and explain why.

itemListElement.name: Fibroids and Fertility Can You Get Pregnant

@graph.name: Fibroids and Fertility Can You Get Pregnant
@graph.headline: Fibroids and Fertility Can You Get Pregnant

mainEntity.name: Can fibroids cause infertility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fibroids can reduce fertility, especially when they grow into the uterine cavity or distort its shape. Many women with fibroids still conceive naturally. A fertility evaluation shows whether fibroids are relevant in your case.

mainEntity.name: Do I need to remove fibroids before IVF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fibroids that distort the uterine cavity are usually treated before IVF because they can reduce implantation success. Small fibroids outside the cavity may not need removal. Your specialist will advise.

mainEntity.name: How long after myomectomy can I try to conceive?

acceptedAnswer.text: The waiting time depends on the type of surgery and how deeply the fibroid extended into the muscle, and is typically a few months. Your surgeon will give specific advice.

mainEntity.name: Can fibroids cause miscarriage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Submucosal fibroids and some large fibroids are linked with higher miscarriage risk. Removing cavity-distorting fibroids before pregnancy may help. Discuss your history with your doctor.

mainEntity.name: Do fibroids shrink on their own?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fibroids can shrink after menopause, and some change in size during pregnancy. During the reproductive years they often remain or grow slowly. Your doctor will monitor and advise.

itemListElement.name: Frozen Embryo Transfer Process and Preparation

@graph.name: Frozen Embryo Transfer Process and Preparation
@graph.headline: Frozen Embryo Transfer Process and Preparation

mainEntity.name: Is frozen embryo transfer better than fresh transfer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Neither is better for everyone. FET offers flexibility and avoids transfer in high-hormone cycles, and for some patients it gives similar or better outcomes. Your doctor will recommend based on your situation.

mainEntity.name: How long can embryos stay frozen?

acceptedAnswer.text: Embryos can remain frozen for many years without losing viability when stored properly. Storage duration is governed by clinic policy and applicable regulations. Your clinic will explain the details.

mainEntity.name: Is frozen embryo transfer painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: The transfer is usually painless or mildly uncomfortable, similar to a Pap smear. You do not need anaesthesia. The hormone medicines may cause side effects such as bloating.

mainEntity.name: When should I take a pregnancy test after FET?

acceptedAnswer.text: A blood pregnancy test is usually done about ten to fourteen days after the transfer, depending on the embryo's stage and your clinic's protocol. Testing too early can give misleading results.

mainEntity.name: Can I resume normal activities after embryo transfer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most people can resume light daily activities soon after transfer, avoiding heavy exercise and straining as advised. Complete bed rest is not required. Follow your doctor's instructions.

itemListElement.name: Genetic Testing in IVF PGT-A Is It Worth It

@graph.name: Genetic Testing in IVF PGT-A Is It Worth It
@graph.headline: Genetic Testing in IVF PGT-A Is It Worth It

mainEntity.name: What is PGT-A in IVF?

acceptedAnswer.text: PGT-A is testing of embryos for an abnormal number of chromosomes before transfer. It aims to help choose embryos with a normal chromosome count, but it does not guarantee a pregnancy and its routine benefit is debated.

mainEntity.name: Does PGT-A improve IVF success?

acceptedAnswer.text: It may help some groups, such as older women or those with recurrent pregnancy loss, by reducing transfers of chromosomally abnormal embryos, but it does not benefit everyone. Your specialist will discuss whether it suits you.

mainEntity.name: Is embryo biopsy safe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Embryo biopsy is performed by experienced embryologists and is considered safe, though a small theoretical risk to the embryo exists. Discuss the details with your clinic.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between PGT-A and PGT-M?

acceptedAnswer.text: PGT-A looks for the wrong number of chromosomes, while PGT-M tests for a specific single-gene disorder that parents carry. Their purposes and indications differ.

mainEntity.name: Do I still need prenatal tests after PGT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. PGT does not detect every condition, so prenatal screening or diagnostic tests may still be recommended. Your doctor will advise during pregnancy.

itemListElement.name: What Happens After Embryo Transfer? Symptoms and Tests

@graph.name: What Happens After Embryo Transfer? Symptoms and Tests
@graph.headline: What Happens After Embryo Transfer? Symptoms and Tests

mainEntity.name: Does cramping after embryo transfer mean the transfer worked?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cramping is common and does not prove that implantation has happened. The uterus can cramp because of the procedure, progesterone, or normal cycle changes. Mild cramping that eases is usually reassuring. Severe, one-sided, or worsening pain should be assessed promptly, whatever the cause.

mainEntity.name: Is spotting after embryo transfer something to worry about?

acceptedAnswer.text: Light spotting is fairly common in the two weeks after transfer, with or without a pregnancy. Heavy bleeding, or bleeding with severe pain or dizziness, needs urgent care. Mention any spotting to your doctor so it can be recorded and reviewed.

mainEntity.name: Can I take a home pregnancy test a few days after transfer?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is better to wait. The trigger injection can leave hCG-like hormone in the body for days, which may cause a false positive. An early test can also miss a real pregnancy. The beta hCG blood test, done 9 to 14 days after transfer, is the most dependable option.

mainEntity.name: Is bed rest necessary after embryo transfer?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Studies have not shown that bed rest improves implantation. Walking and normal daily routines are generally fine. Avoid heavy lifting and strenuous exercise until your doctor confirms it is safe for you.

mainEntity.name: Where can I get post-transfer care in East Bangalore?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dr. Swati Shree at EVE Women and Fertility Clinic in Gunjur, Bangalore, offers fertility consultations and follow-up guidance, including for patients whose IVF cycles were done at partner centres. Gunjur is close to Varthur and Whitefield. Bring your transfer details, current medicine list, and recent blood reports to the appointment.

itemListElement.name: How Long Does IVF Take? The Real Timeline

@graph.name: How Long Does IVF Take? Timeline to Pregnancy Test
@graph.headline: How Long Does IVF Take? Timeline to Pregnancy Test

mainEntity.name: How long does IVF take from the first injection to the pregnancy test?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a fresh cycle, the active treatment window is 8 to 14 days of injections, a trigger shot, egg collection about 34 to 36 hours later, three to five days of embryo growth, and a beta hCG test 9 to 14 days after transfer. Together these stages usually add up to four to six weeks. Your schedule may be shorter or longer depending on how your ovaries respond.

mainEntity.name: How long does the whole IVF process take from the first consultation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Counting consultation, blood tests, scans and semen analysis, most couples should set aside six to ten weeks. Occasionally a procedure such as a hysteroscopy comes first, which adds time. Tests that must be repeated on specific cycle days can also shift the start date. A written schedule from the first visit makes it easier to plan leave.

mainEntity.name: Why does a frozen embryo transfer take longer?

acceptedAnswer.text: A frozen transfer means the embryos are stored and placed in a later cycle. The lining must be prepared first, either through a natural cycle or with hormone tablets, and that preparation typically adds a month or more. Doctors often suggest this route when the ovaries responded strongly, when OHSS risk is a concern, or when embryo testing is planned.

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to take a home pregnancy test before the blood test?

acceptedAnswer.text: Waiting for the scheduled blood test gives the clearest answer. The trigger shot can leave a hormone similar to hCG in the body for several days, so an early home test may read positive without a pregnancy. A test taken too soon can also read negative even when a pregnancy has started. Report any worrying symptoms to your clinic rather than relying on a home kit.

mainEntity.name: Where can I get IVF timeline guidance in East Bangalore?

acceptedAnswer.text: Gunjur sits in East Bangalore, close to Varthur and Whitefield. EVE Women and Fertility Clinic offers fertility consultations there, and IVF treatment can be guided through partner fertility centres in Bangalore. Bringing previous test reports to the first visit lets the timeline reflect your own situation.

@graph.name: How Long to Try Before Seeing a Fertility Specialist
@graph.headline: How Long to Try Before Seeing a Fertility Specialist

mainEntity.name: How long should we try before seeing a fertility doctor?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the woman is under 35, after 12 months of trying. If she is 35 or older, after 6 months. If she is over 40, see a specialist promptly.

mainEntity.name: Should we see a specialist sooner if periods are irregular?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Irregular or absent periods may indicate ovulation problems such as PCOS, so evaluation should happen sooner.

mainEntity.name: Does the male partner need testing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Male factors contribute to many infertility cases. A semen analysis is a simple, important early test.

mainEntity.name: Can we see a fertility specialist before trying?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A preconception consultation can review health, check basic fertility markers and give advice to improve your chances.

mainEntity.name: How often should we have intercourse when trying?

acceptedAnswer.text: Intercourse every two to three days throughout the cycle, or more often around ovulation, gives a good chance of conception without needing perfect timing.

itemListElement.name: How Many IUI Cycles Should You Try Before IVF?

@graph.name: How Many IUI Cycles Should You Try Before IVF?
@graph.headline: How Many IUI Cycles Should You Try Before IVF?

mainEntity.name: How many IUI cycles should I try?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many specialists suggest up to about three to four cycles for suitable couples. Older women or those with other fertility factors may move to IVF sooner.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth trying more than four IUI cycles?

acceptedAnswer.text: The chance per cycle tends to fall after the first few attempts. Some couples continue, but many are advised to consider IVF. Discuss with your specialist.

mainEntity.name: Should women over 35 try IUI?

acceptedAnswer.text: IUI may be tried in some women over 35 with suitable conditions, but fewer cycles are often advised before moving to IVF because of age-related fertility decline.

mainEntity.name: Why did my IUI fail?

acceptedAnswer.text: IUI may not work because of egg or sperm factors, timing, unexplained factors or age. It does not always mean something is wrong. Your specialist will review and suggest next steps.

mainEntity.name: When should we go directly to IVF?

acceptedAnswer.text: IVF is often recommended directly for blocked tubes, significant male factor infertility, older age, low ovarian reserve or severe endometriosis.

itemListElement.name: Hysteroscopy for Infertility When Is It Needed

@graph.name: Hysteroscopy for Infertility When Is It Needed
@graph.headline: Hysteroscopy for Infertility When Is It Needed

mainEntity.name: Is hysteroscopy painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: Diagnostic hysteroscopy may cause mild to moderate cramping, and many women tolerate it well in a clinic. Operative procedures are usually done under sedation or anaesthesia, so you feel little during the procedure.

mainEntity.name: Does hysteroscopy improve fertility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Removing polyps, fibroids that distort the cavity, scar tissue or a septum can improve the uterine environment and may improve the chance of implantation in selected women. It does not help everyone.

mainEntity.name: When can I try to conceive after hysteroscopy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many women can try in the next cycle or after a short interval, depending on what was done. Your doctor will give specific advice, particularly after removing fibroids or scar tissue.

mainEntity.name: Do I need hysteroscopy before IVF?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not for everyone. It may be advised if scans suggest cavity problems, after repeated implantation failure or when otherwise indicated. Your specialist will decide.

mainEntity.name: What are the risks of hysteroscopy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Risks are uncommon and include infection, bleeding and, rarely, uterine perforation or fluid overload. Seek help for fever, heavy bleeding or severe pain after the procedure.

@graph.name: ICSI for Male Infertility: When Is It Recommended?
@graph.headline: ICSI for Male Infertility: When Is It Recommended?

mainEntity.name: Is ICSI the same as IVF?

acceptedAnswer.text: ICSI is a technique used within IVF. The main difference is how fertilisation happens. In standard IVF, sperm fertilise the egg on their own. In ICSI, a single sperm is injected directly into each egg.

mainEntity.name: Does ICSI improve pregnancy chances?

acceptedAnswer.text: ICSI improves fertilisation when there is significant male infertility. It does not usually improve pregnancy chances when sperm are normal. Pregnancy still depends on egg quality, embryo development and the uterus.

mainEntity.name: Is ICSI painful for the woman?

acceptedAnswer.text: The ICSI step happens in the lab, so it causes no extra pain. The woman goes through the same IVF steps, including stimulation and egg collection, which is done under sedation.

mainEntity.name: Can ICSI be used with surgically retrieved sperm?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Sperm collected from the testis or epididymis are usually few and less mobile, so ICSI is the standard way to use them for fertilisation.

mainEntity.name: Are babies born through ICSI healthy?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most babies born through ICSI are healthy. Some small increased risks have been reported, which may be linked to the father's infertility itself. Your doctor can discuss genetic counselling if needed.

mainEntity.name: Will ICSI fix poor sperm DNA quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: ICSI helps sperm enter the egg, but it does not repair damaged DNA. In some cases, doctors may suggest lifestyle changes, treatment of causes or using testicular sperm. Results vary.

@graph.headline: IUI Success Factors: Age, Ovulation and Sperm Quality

mainEntity.name: What is the best age for IUI?

acceptedAnswer.text: IUI generally has better outcomes in younger women because egg quality is higher. Women over 35 can still benefit, but specialists may suggest fewer IUI cycles before considering IVF. Age is always weighed with other test results.

mainEntity.name: Does sperm count matter for IUI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The number of moving sperm after washing is an important factor. If counts are very low, IUI may not be the best option, and IVF with ICSI may be considered instead.

mainEntity.name: Do both tubes need to be open for IUI?

acceptedAnswer.text: At least one healthy, open tube is needed. If both tubes are blocked, IUI cannot work because the egg and sperm cannot meet. A tubal test is usually done before planning IUI.

mainEntity.name: Does ovulation medicine improve IUI outcomes?

acceptedAnswer.text: In many couples, mild ovulation medicines with monitoring can improve IUI outcomes by ensuring an egg is ready at the right time. They are used carefully to avoid too many follicles.

mainEntity.name: Can lifestyle changes improve IUI success?

acceptedAnswer.text: Healthy habits support fertility for both partners. Stopping smoking, limiting alcohol, keeping a healthy weight and managing health conditions may help. They do not change age-related factors.

mainEntity.name: Can stress affect IUI results?

acceptedAnswer.text: Stress is common during fertility treatment. Its direct effect on IUI outcomes is uncertain, but managing stress improves well-being. Counselling, gentle exercise and support from your partner can help.

@graph.name: IUI Treatment: Complete Guide to Intrauterine Insemination
@graph.headline: IUI Treatment: Complete Guide to Intrauterine Insemination

mainEntity.name: What is IUI treatment and how does it work?

acceptedAnswer.text: IUI treatment involves placing specially prepared sperm directly into the uterus around the time of ovulation. The procedure does not involve laboratory fertilisation. After insemination, sperm still needs to reach and fertilise an egg naturally. IUI may be considered when the fertility assessment suggests that this approach has a reasonable chance of helping.

mainEntity.name: Does IUI hurt?

acceptedAnswer.text: IUI is usually a brief procedure. Some women experience mild cramping, pressure or light spotting when the catheter passes through the cervix. Others experience very little discomfort. Severe or persistent pain is not expected after a routine procedure and should be discussed with the treating fertility team.

mainEntity.name: How soon after IUI can you take a pregnancy test?

acceptedAnswer.text: The appropriate testing date depends on when ovulation occurred and whether an hCG trigger was used. Testing very early can be misleading because an hCG trigger may temporarily affect the result. Your fertility clinic will usually provide a specific date for pregnancy testing, and a blood beta-hCG test may be used when confirmation is needed.

mainEntity.name: How many IUI cycles are usually needed?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no fixed number of IUI cycles for every patient. The decision depends on age, diagnosis, ovarian reserve, sperm quality, tubal status and the response to previous treatment. For selected couples with unexplained infertility, a limited course of stimulated IUI may be considered before IVF, but treatment should be individualised.

mainEntity.name: Can women with PCOS have IUI?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, IUI can be considered for selected women with PCOS. Since PCOS can cause irregular or absent ovulation, treatment may first focus on inducing or supporting ovulation and monitoring follicle development. Whether IUI is appropriate also depends on sperm quality, fallopian-tube status, age and other fertility factors.

mainEntity.name: Is IUI better than IVF?

acceptedAnswer.text: IUI and IVF serve different purposes. IUI places prepared sperm inside the uterus, while IVF involves retrieving eggs and fertilising them in a laboratory. IUI may be appropriate for some couples, while IVF may be more suitable when there are factors such as significant sperm problems, blocked tubes or other fertility concerns.

mainEntity.name: Where can I get IUI treatment in Bangalore?

acceptedAnswer.text: EVE Women and Fertility Clinic in Gunjur, Bangalore provides fertility assessment, ovulation induction, follicle monitoring and IUI within its stated ART Level 1 scope. A consultation with Dr. Swati Shree can help determine whether IUI fits your fertility history and what investigations may be needed before treatment. Pasted text(20261003-114820)

@graph.headline: IUI vs IVF: Which Fertility Treatment Is Considered When?

mainEntity.name: What is the main difference between IUI and IVF?

acceptedAnswer.text: In IUI, sperm is placed in the uterus and fertilisation happens inside the body. In IVF, eggs are collected and fertilised in a laboratory, and an embryo is transferred to the uterus.

mainEntity.name: Is IUI or IVF more successful?

acceptedAnswer.text: IVF generally has higher success rates per cycle than IUI. However, IUI may be appropriate for some couples because it is simpler and less intensive.

mainEntity.name: Can I have IUI if my tubes are blocked?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. IUI requires at least one open fallopian tube. IVF bypasses the tubes and is usually recommended for blocked tubes.

mainEntity.name: Should I try IUI before IVF?

acceptedAnswer.text: For some couples, such as those with mild male factor or unexplained infertility and younger age, a few IUI cycles may be tried first. Others may be advised to go directly to IVF.

mainEntity.name: Is IUI painful?

acceptedAnswer.text: IUI is usually quick and causes only mild discomfort, similar to a Pap smear. Some women have mild cramping afterward.

@graph.headline: Trying to Conceive After 35: When to Consider IVF

mainEntity.name: Should I go straight to IVF at 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not always. If your egg reserve is good, tubes are open and sperm is normal, simpler treatments may be tried for a short time. Your specialist will consider all factors before advising IVF.

mainEntity.name: How many IUI cycles should I try after 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often fewer than younger women, because time is important. Many specialists suggest a limited number of well-timed IUI cycles before discussing IVF. The exact number depends on your results.

mainEntity.name: Is IVF more successful than IUI after 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: IVF usually offers a higher chance per cycle than IUI, especially when other factors are present. However, it is more intensive and costly. The best option depends on your diagnosis and age.

mainEntity.name: Does low AMH mean I need IVF immediately?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low AMH means fewer eggs remain, so specialists often suggest moving to treatment sooner. It does not always mean IVF is the only option. Your age and other results guide the choice.

mainEntity.name: Can I freeze embryos during IVF for later?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Extra good-quality embryos can often be frozen for future use. This may help couples plan a second child or another attempt without repeating stimulation.

mainEntity.name: Is genetic testing of embryos needed after 35?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is not essential for everyone. PGT-A may be discussed for women over 35, especially with recurrent miscarriage or failed IVF. Your specialist will explain the benefits and limitations.

@graph.name: IVF Process Step by Step in Bangalore
@graph.headline: IVF Process Step by Step in Bangalore

mainEntity.name: How long does the IVF process take from the first consultation to embryo transfer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tests and planning often take two to four weeks, sometimes longer. Stimulation then runs for 8 to 14 days, and collection happens about 34 to 36 hours after the trigger shot. A fresh transfer follows 3 to 5 days later. Altogether, a fresh cycle takes around four to six weeks from the first injection to the pregnancy test. Frozen transfers take longer because they happen in a later cycle.

mainEntity.name: Do I have to start IVF right after the first consultation?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your results. Your doctor reviews the tests first and may suggest ovulation tablets or IUI, depending on your diagnosis, age and how long you have been trying. Some couples go directly to IVF, for instance when both tubes are blocked or sperm problems are severe. Ask for a written plan and cost estimate before any medicine is started.

mainEntity.name: Does egg collection hurt?

acceptedAnswer.text: The procedure is done under sedation or light anaesthesia, so you won't feel it. Cramping and light spotting for a day or two are common afterwards. Ask your clinic which pain relief is safe for you. Heavy bleeding, fever or severe belly pain after collection should be assessed promptly.

mainEntity.name: Why are there fewer embryos than eggs collected?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not every follicle contains an egg, and some collected eggs are immature and cannot be fertilised. After fertilisation, some embryos stop dividing during the three to five days in culture. Early embryo loss also happens in natural conception. Your embryologist will tell you which embryos are developing well enough for transfer or freezing.

mainEntity.name: Can I take a home pregnancy test after embryo transfer?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is better to wait for the blood test, done 9 to 14 days after transfer. The trigger injection can leave hormone traces that cause a false positive early on, and testing too soon can also miss a pregnancy. If you notice bleeding or symptoms in the meantime, call your doctor rather than testing again and again. Keep taking progesterone until your team advises otherwise.

mainEntity.name: Where can I get an IVF evaluation in East Bangalore?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dr. Swati Shree consults at EVE Women and Fertility Clinic in Gunjur, Bangalore, which is within easy reach of Varthur, Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Bellandur. Where IVF is recommended, she guides treatment through partner fertility centres in Bangalore, including Apollo Fertility and Motherhood Fertility, where she is a visiting consultant. A consultation lets her build the plan around your own reports.

mainEntity.name: Which factor matters most for IVF success?

acceptedAnswer.text: Age, almost every time. As a woman gets older, both the number of eggs and the share with normal chromosomes tend to drop. That affects how many embryos develop well and how likely they are to implant. Egg reserve, sperm quality, uterine health and embryo grade still matter, and your doctor weighs them together with age.

mainEntity.name: Can IVF work with a low AMH?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often, yes, though the approach may differ. A low AMH usually predicts fewer eggs in a cycle, so the stimulation plan may be adjusted. AMH does not measure egg quality, and a few healthy eggs can still lead to pregnancy. Your age, antral follicle count and other results help your doctor set realistic expectations.

mainEntity.name: Does a weak semen report mean IVF will fail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Rarely on its own. A semen report below WHO reference values tells the team that sperm need extra support. ICSI can work around many problems with count, movement and shape, because one selected sperm is placed into each egg. Depending on the findings, your doctor may recommend lifestyle changes, treatment for an underlying cause or further testing.

mainEntity.name: Should every IVF embryo be tested for chromosomes?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not for everyone. ESHRE and ASRM do not recommend routine testing for all patients. It may be considered for older women, couples with repeated pregnancy loss, or those with several unsuccessful transfers. Testing involves an embryo biopsy and has its own limits, so weigh the benefits, costs and drawbacks with your doctor before agreeing to it.

mainEntity.name: Do lifestyle changes make a real difference?

acceptedAnswer.text: They can, especially for sperm and the uterine lining. Quitting smoking, cutting back on alcohol, reaching a healthy weight and keeping thyroid disease or diabetes under control all help. Skip herbal powders and supplements your doctor has not prescribed, because some can interfere with IVF medicines or affect the body in unexpected ways.

mainEntity.name: Where can I get an IVF evaluation in East Bangalore?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dr. Swati Shree sees patients at EVE Women and Fertility Clinic in Gunjur, a practical choice for people in Varthur, Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Bellandur. She evaluates both partners at EVE. If IVF is the right next step, she guides treatment through her partner fertility centres in Bangalore, so the same doctor follows you from start to finish.

mainEntity.name: Does IVF hurt?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most of IVF involves only mild discomfort. The daily injections feel like a quick pinch, and many women give them at home after a nurse shows them how. Egg collection is done under sedation or light anaesthesia, so you won't feel it, though cramping afterwards is common. Embryo transfer feels much like a Pap smear and usually needs no anaesthesia.

mainEntity.name: How many days of injections does IVF need?

acceptedAnswer.text: Stimulation injections usually run for 8 to 14 days. The exact number depends on your ovarian reserve and how your ovaries respond, which your doctor tracks with scans every few days. When the follicles are ready, you get a trigger injection, and egg collection follows about 34 to 36 hours later.

mainEntity.name: Do I need bed rest after embryo transfer?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Research hasn't found that lying in bed after transfer improves the chance of pregnancy. Most women go back to light routine activities, including office work, within a day or so. It's sensible to skip heavy lifting and strenuous workouts for a while, and to follow any specific advice your fertility team gives you.

mainEntity.name: Can IVF work if my AMH is low?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can. Low AMH usually means fewer eggs are collected in each cycle, but AMH doesn't measure egg quality, and it doesn't rule out pregnancy. Your doctor may change the stimulation plan to suit a lower reserve. Your age and other test results also shape your chances, so a personal consultation gives the clearest picture.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between IVF and ICSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: In standard IVF, each egg is placed in a dish with many sperm and fertilisation happens on its own. In ICSI, an embryologist injects a single sperm directly into each mature egg. ICSI is done as part of an IVF cycle, usually for a low sperm count, poor sperm movement, or poor fertilisation in an earlier attempt.

mainEntity.name: When can I take a pregnancy test after IVF?

acceptedAnswer.text: The beta hCG blood test is usually done 9 to 14 days after embryo transfer, depending on the embryo's stage and your clinic's advice. Home tests taken earlier can mislead you. The trigger injection may cause a false positive in the first days, and testing too soon can also give a false negative.

acceptedAnswer.text: Dr. Swati Shree consults at EVE Women and Fertility Clinic in Gunjur, which is convenient from Varthur, Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and Bellandur. She evaluates couples at EVE, and when IVF is needed she manages treatment through her partner fertility centres in Bangalore, so the same specialist oversees your care from start to finish.

@graph.headline: Letrozole for PCOS and How It Can Help You Conceive

mainEntity.name: Is letrozole given as an injection?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Letrozole is an oral tablet. Your doctor sets the dose and number of days based on your cycle history, blood tests and ultrasound findings. Injections enter the picture only in certain plans, usually when the ovary does not respond well to tablets. Do not start letrozole without a prescription, even if a friend or an online source suggests it.

mainEntity.name: How long before you know whether letrozole has worked?

acceptedAnswer.text: The response is usually judged across one or more cycles. Follicular scans and symptoms show whether ovulation occurred, and a pregnancy test is taken at the recommended time, typically about two weeks after ovulation. A cycle without pregnancy is common and does not signal permanent failure. Your doctor will review what happened before recommending the next step.

mainEntity.name: Is letrozole with IUI available in Bangalore?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for suitable couples. It is often used alongside IUI when ovulation can be induced and tracked on scans, and when semen quality and tubal status look appropriate. EVE Women and Fertility Clinic in Gunjur offers ovulation induction, follicle monitoring and IUI within its ART Level 1 scope. Patients from East Bangalore can book a consultation with Dr. Swati Shree to discuss whether this suits them.

mainEntity.name: What happens if letrozole does not lead to pregnancy?

acceptedAnswer.text: The next step depends on what the cycles showed. Options can include adjusting the dosing schedule, adding closer monitoring, moving to IUI, or checking other factors such as sperm quality and the fallopian tubes. IVF is usually discussed when ovulation treatments have not worked or another factor makes it more appropriate. Advanced IVF procedures are carried out through EVE's partner fertility centres.

mainEntity.name: Can letrozole be used for irregular periods without PCOS?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be considered, but only once the cause is clear. Irregular periods may stem from thyroid disease, raised prolactin or other hormonal conditions, and these need investigation first. If a specialist confirms that ovulation is the problem, letrozole may be an option. The decision rests on your full clinical picture, not on your period pattern alone.

mainEntity.name: Can IVF work with low AMH?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. IVF can work with low AMH, though fewer eggs are usually collected. Success depends strongly on age and egg quality, and treatment is tailored to your response.

mainEntity.name: How many eggs can I expect with low AMH?

acceptedAnswer.text: Egg numbers vary widely depending on AMH, age, antral follicle count and protocol. Your specialist can give a personalised estimate after assessment.

mainEntity.name: Does low AMH mean my IVF cycle will fail?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not necessarily. Low AMH predicts quantity, not quality. Younger women with low AMH can still achieve pregnancy with good-quality eggs.

mainEntity.name: Should I do multiple IVF cycles with low AMH?

acceptedAnswer.text: Some patients benefit from more than one stimulation cycle to accumulate eggs or embryos. Your specialist will discuss whether this suits you.

mainEntity.name: When are donor eggs considered?

acceptedAnswer.text: Donor eggs may be considered when ovarian response is very low, repeated cycles have not succeeded or age significantly affects egg quality. This is a personal decision made after counselling.

mainEntity.name: What does low AMH mean at age 30?

acceptedAnswer.text: It suggests fewer eggs than typical for your age, but egg quality is usually still good. Natural conception is often possible, and early specialist evaluation helps with planning.

mainEntity.name: Is low AMH at 35 a concern?

acceptedAnswer.text: It means time matters more. Seek specialist evaluation sooner and discuss timelines for natural trying or treatment, as egg quality also begins to decline with age.

mainEntity.name: Can I get pregnant at 40 with low AMH?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is possible, but chances are lower and miscarriage risk is higher because egg quality declines with age. Prompt specialist advice on options such as IVF or donor eggs is important.

mainEntity.name: Does AMH decrease every year?

acceptedAnswer.text: AMH generally declines with age, though individual results can vary between tests. Your specialist will interpret trends alongside other tests.

mainEntity.name: Should I freeze my eggs if I have low AMH at 30?

acceptedAnswer.text: If you are not planning pregnancy soon, egg freezing may be worth discussing. Earlier freezing generally gives better outcomes.

@graph.headline: Low AMH & Ovarian Reserve: Fertility Explained

mainEntity.name: Can I get pregnant naturally with low AMH?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Low AMH does not automatically prevent natural pregnancy. AMH mainly provides information about ovarian reserve. Age, ovulation, fallopian tubes, sperm factors, endometriosis, uterine factors and the length of time you have been trying to conceive also influence fertility.

mainEntity.name: Does low AMH mean poor egg quality?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AMH is primarily a marker of ovarian reserve and does not directly measure egg quality. Egg quality is strongly influenced by age, and there is no routine blood test that can directly determine the genetic quality of individual eggs.

mainEntity.name: Is IVF possible with low AMH?

acceptedAnswer.text: IVF may still be considered when AMH is low. A low AMH can suggest that the ovaries may produce fewer eggs during stimulation, which can affect treatment planning. However, AMH alone does not determine whether an IVF cycle will result in pregnancy.

mainEntity.name: Can low AMH be increased naturally?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no established treatment that can restore eggs that have already been lost or create a new ovarian reserve. Healthy lifestyle choices support general health, but they should not be presented as a way to reverse reduced ovarian reserve. Fertility decisions should be based on proper medical assessment.

mainEntity.name: Is AMH the same as antral follicle count?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. AMH is measured through a blood test, while antral follicle count is assessed using transvaginal ultrasound. Both provide information about ovarian reserve and may be considered together when planning fertility treatment.

mainEntity.name: Does low AMH cause miscarriage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Low AMH should not be considered a direct cause of miscarriage. AMH primarily reflects ovarian reserve. Pregnancy loss has multiple possible causes, and age-related egg quality and chromosomal factors are considered separately when assessing fertility and pregnancy history.

mainEntity.name: Should I worry about low AMH at 35 or 40?

acceptedAnswer.text: A low AMH at 35 or 40 should be interpreted alongside age rather than by itself. Both ovarian reserve and age-related changes in egg quality can be relevant. A fertility specialist can review AMH, AFC, menstrual history and other factors to discuss appropriate reproductive planning.

mainEntity.name: Where can I get a low AMH fertility consultation in Bangalore?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fertility consultation with Dr. Swati Shree is available at EVE Women and Fertility Clinic in Gunjur, Bangalore. The consultation can help assess low AMH alongside age, ovarian reserve, menstrual history and other relevant fertility factors.

@graph.name: Low Sperm Count: Natural and Medical Treatment Options
@graph.headline: Low Sperm Count: Natural and Medical Treatment Options

mainEntity.name: How long does it take to improve sperm count?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sperm take about 70 to 90 days to develop. Any lifestyle or medical changes need at least three months to show in a semen analysis. Your doctor may repeat the test after this time.

mainEntity.name: Can diet improve sperm count?

acceptedAnswer.text: A balanced diet supports overall health and may help sperm quality. Fruits, vegetables, whole grains, nuts and lean protein are good choices. Diet alone may not fix a medical cause, so evaluation is still important.

mainEntity.name: Does testosterone help low sperm count?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Testosterone supplements usually lower sperm production by signalling the body to stop making its own hormones. They should not be used to treat male infertility unless a specialist advises it for a specific reason.

mainEntity.name: Can a varicocele be the cause of low sperm count?

acceptedAnswer.text: It can be in some men. A varicocele may raise testicular temperature and affect sperm. Repair may help selected men with abnormal semen. Not every varicocele needs treatment.

mainEntity.name: Can a man with very low sperm count become a father?

acceptedAnswer.text: Often yes. IVF with ICSI needs only a small number of healthy sperm. Even when no sperm are in the semen, sperm can sometimes be retrieved surgically. A specialist will explain the options.

mainEntity.name: Are fertility supplements for men effective?

acceptedAnswer.text: Evidence for antioxidants and fertility supplements is mixed. They may help some men but are not a cure. Speak with your doctor before using them and avoid products that promise guaranteed results.

mainEntity.name: Can a man with a low sperm count still father a child?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many men with a low count do become fathers, some naturally and some with treatment. A lot depends on how low the count is, how well the sperm move, what is causing the problem and how fertile the female partner is. Milder cases may respond to lifestyle changes, treatment of the cause or IUI. Severe cases often move to IVF with ICSI.

mainEntity.name: How many days of abstinence are needed before a semen analysis?

acceptedAnswer.text: The WHO recommends 2 to 7 days without ejaculation before giving a sample. Too short a gap tends to lower the count, while a very long gap leaves more old, slow sperm in the sample. Collect the whole ejaculate in the sterile container from the lab, and avoid lubricants, saliva and ordinary condoms, since these can damage sperm.

mainEntity.name: Does a normal semen analysis mean a man is definitely fertile?

acceptedAnswer.text: A normal report is reassuring but not a guarantee. The test measures count, movement and shape, and it cannot fully judge whether sperm will fertilise an egg. In the other direction, results a little below the reference limits don't rule out a natural pregnancy. Doctors read the report together with the couple's history and the woman's test results.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between IVF and ICSI?

acceptedAnswer.text: With standard IVF, eggs and prepared sperm are placed together in a lab dish and the sperm fertilise the eggs on their own. With ICSI, an embryologist injects one sperm directly into each mature egg. ICSI is usually chosen for severe male infertility, for surgically retrieved sperm, or after eggs failed to fertilise in an earlier IVF cycle. The woman's side of treatment is the same for both.

mainEntity.name: Does every varicocele need surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Most men with a varicocele have normal fertility and need nothing done. Surgery may be considered when the varicocele can be felt on examination, the semen report is abnormal and the couple is trying to conceive. The woman's age also matters, because waiting several months for semen to improve after surgery does not suit every couple. A urologist usually makes this call.

mainEntity.name: Can gym supplements or testosterone injections lower sperm count?

acceptedAnswer.text: They can, and often quite sharply. Testosterone injections, anabolic steroids and some gym products with hidden steroids signal the brain to stop driving sperm production, sometimes down to zero. Production frequently comes back after stopping, though it may take months. Anyone on prescribed testosterone should speak to their doctor before stopping it.

mainEntity.name: Where can couples get a fertility evaluation in East Bangalore?

acceptedAnswer.text: Couples from Gunjur, Varthur, Whitefield, Sarjapur Road and nearby areas can see Dr. Swati Shree at EVE Women and Fertility Clinic in Gunjur, Bangalore. The consultation looks at both partners, including guidance on the semen analysis, and EVE provides follicle monitoring and IUI. When IVF or ICSI is needed, she guides treatment through her partner fertility centres in Bangalore.

mainEntity.name: Does a man need a separate doctor for male infertility?

acceptedAnswer.text: The first visit is often with a fertility specialist who sees both partners and reviews the semen report. If it points to something significant, such as no sperm, a varicocele, a hormone problem or a possible blockage, the next step may be a urologist or andrologist. These specialists handle male examinations, surgery and sperm retrieval procedures.

@graph.headline: Male Infertility: Causes, Symptoms and When to Seek Help

mainEntity.name: Can a man look healthy and still be infertile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Most men with low sperm count or poor motility feel completely normal and have normal sexual function. A semen analysis is the only reliable way to check sperm health.

mainEntity.name: What lifestyle habits reduce male fertility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Smoking, heavy alcohol, recreational drugs, obesity, long exposure to heat and anabolic steroids can all reduce sperm quality. Improving these habits may help, though changes take around three months to show.

mainEntity.name: Does age affect male fertility?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but more gradually than in women. Sperm quality and DNA integrity may decline with age, especially after the mid-forties. Age is one factor among many in a couple's evaluation.

mainEntity.name: Can male infertility be treated?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many causes can be treated or improved, such as hormone problems, varicocele or lifestyle factors. When treatment is not enough, IUI or IVF with ICSI can help couples conceive.

mainEntity.name: Should men be tested before women start fertility treatment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ideally, both partners should be tested at the start. A semen analysis is simple and low-cost, and its results can change which treatment is suitable for the couple.

mainEntity.name: Can stress affect sperm?

acceptedAnswer.text: Long-term stress may affect hormones and sexual function, which can influence fertility. Managing stress through sleep, exercise and support is helpful, but it is not usually the only cause of male infertility.
